headline: Roche payout swings Sarepta to profit despite ELEVIDYS drop
summary_short: Sarepta's Q1 total revenue fell 1.9% y/y to $730.8 million as ELEVIDYS product sales dropped 72.8% to $102.0 million, but $400.3 million of Roche collaboration payments (including $325.0 million for a declined option) swung the company to $331.0 million of net income versus a $447.5 million loss a year ago.
summary_long: Net product revenue fell 46% y/y to $330.5 million, driven by ELEVIDYS (-73% to $102.0 million) as post-2025-safety-event demand and the ambulatory-only label update cut volume; PMO products were roughly flat (-3%) at $228.6 million. Collaboration revenue nearly tripled to $400.3 million on $325.0 million from Roche's declined program-rights option plus a $40.0 million Japan-dosing milestone. R&D fell 80% to $154.0 million, mainly because Q1 2025 included a $583.6 million Arrowhead upfront payment; SG&A fell 18% on lower commercialization spend and headcount after the 2025 restructuring. This drove a swing to $358.4 million operating income and $331.0 million net income ($2.88 diluted EPS). Cash fell to $464.5 million from $801.3 million on an Arrowhead DM1 milestone and working-capital swings.
confidence_notes: force-regenerated summary, replacing a prior version. Net income swing is dominated by non-recurring items on both sides of the comparison: $365.0M of one-time Roche collaboration revenue (declined-option + Japan milestone) in Q1 2026 vs. a $583.6M Arrowhead upfront R&D charge in Q1 2025 — underlying ELEVIDYS commercial trends remain negative. Operating income/net income/diluted EPS q/q and y/y deltas omitted (marked delta_basis: none) because the prior-period base was a loss, making a percentage delta not meaningful (filing itself marks this '*Not meaningful').

drivers.explanation: Decline driven by lower sales volume reflecting demand changes following 2025 safety events and the subsequent label update restricting treatment to the ambulatory patient population.
$325.0M recognized for Roche's declined option to acquire program rights (previously deferred revenue) plus a $40.0M milestone for first commercial ELEVIDYS dosing in Japan.

Prior-year quarter included a $583.6M Arrowhead upfront license fee; partially offset by a new $50.0M annual Arrowhead collaboration fee in Q1 2026. Also lower manufacturing, headcount and clinical-trial costs from the 2025 Pipeline Reprioritization and Restructuring.

Cost of sales fell 21% (also volume-driven, partly offset by scrapped/expired materials and quality write-offs) while collaboration revenue nearly tripled, lifting the consolidated margin despite falling product sales.

Fell on a $200.0M DM1 milestone payment and $50.0M annual license fee to Arrowhead, a $274.9M deferred-revenue drawdown, and a $210.5M accounts-payable decrease including the Arrowhead milestone payment.

Reported net income was driven by one-time Roche collaboration payments and the absence of the prior year's large Arrowhead upfront charge, not by underlying ELEVIDYS commercial recovery, which continued to decline.
